=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves attach at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or clustered attachment visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with visible internodes, not clustered at the apex)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly curved, not tapered or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible and run parallel to each other, close together)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface has a glossy appearance, likely due to moisture but inherent sheen is present)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short compared to leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly thickened, with visible lenticels, suggesting woody tissue)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: dark green to brownish (stem is dark green with some brownish or grayish patches, possibly due to moisture or lichen)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): lenticellate (small, raised, corky spots visible on stem surface, consistent with lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no structures visible at leaf base that resemble stipules)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no milky or clear sap exuding from cut surfaces or wounds)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base or petiole, which would indicate pulvinus)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no modified stems or leaves functioning as tendrils)

F. Notes: Some leaves show minor damage with holes and irregular margins, possibly due to physical disturbance or minor herbivory; overall plant appears to be a small seedling with multiple stems emerging from ground level. Leaf surfaces are wet, likely due to recent rain, which enhances shine and may obscure some fine features. No flowers or fruits are visible. The plant is growing among leaf litter, with other small plants and ferns in close proximity. A pink tag is visible near the base, likely for research or monitoring purposes.
